question: Which festival is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Milad-un-Nabi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Milad-un-Nabi**, also known as Mawlid, is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad, the founder of Islam.
 
• It is observed on the **12th day of the Islamic month of Rabi-ul-Awwal**, as per the Hijri lunar calendar.
 
• The festival is marked by **prayers, sermons, and recitations** of the Quran, focusing on the life and teachings of Prophet Muhammad.
 
• Muslims across the world organize religious gatherings, processions, and charitable activities on this day.
 
• The event is particularly significant for Sunni Muslims, while many Shia Muslims celebrate the birth of the Prophet on a different date.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prophet Muhammad:**

 
 
• Born in **570 CE** in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, Prophet Muhammad is considered the last prophet in Islam.
 
• He received revelations from Allah through the angel Gabriel, which are compiled in the Islamic holy book, the Quran.
 
 
 
• **Rabi-ul-Awwal:**
 
 
• It is the third month in the Islamic lunar calendar and holds religious significance for Muslims.
 
• Several important events in the Prophet's life, including his migration from Mecca to Medina, occurred in this month.
 
 
 
• **Celebration Practices:**
 
 
• Milad-un-Nabi is celebrated differently across countries, with traditions varying from region to region.
 
• In some places, people decorate streets, mosques, and homes with lights and banners.
 
• Charitable acts, such as distributing food and clothing to the needy, are emphasized during the festival.
 
 
 
• **Controversies:**
 
 
• While many Muslims celebrate Milad-un-Nabi, some Islamic scholars and groups believe that such celebrations are not part of the original teachings of Islam.
 
• These debates revolve around the permissibility of innovations (bid'ah) in religious practices.
